another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

First, could you tell me: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex. He lives at home with me, and I live here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know that you have one child, Alex, who lives with you in the UK.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you some questions:

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure of his exact age at the moment - he's somewhere between 15 and 19. I can get you his exact birthdate if you need it, but I know he's in that age range.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. The exact age is important because there are specific age-related rules for Child Benefit eligibility, particularly around age 16 and when a young person turns 20.

**Could you please provide Alex's exact date of birth, or at least confirm whether he is:**
- **Under 16 years old, or**
- **16 years old or over?**

If he's 16 or over, I'll also need to know about his education or training status, as this affects eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I understand the age matters, but I honestly don't have his exact birthdate with me right now. I know he's definitely somewhere in that 15 to 19 range, but I can't tell you for certain whether he's just turned 16 or not. Is there a way we can work through this, or do I need to come back with his exact date of birth?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I appreciate your honesty. While I can help you understand the general rules, I do need to know whether Alex is under 16 or 16 and over, as the eligibility criteria are different for these age groups.

Let me explain why this matters:

- **For children under 16:** Child Benefit is generally available without additional conditions related to education or training.
- **For young people aged 16-19:** Child Benefit can continue, but only if they're in approved education or training.

**Given that you know Alex is between 15 and 19, can you at least tell me:**

1. **Is Alex still in school or college, or is he in any form of approved education or training?**

This information, combined with knowing his approximate age, will help me give you a better indication of eligibility. However, for a definitive assessment, you would eventually need to confirm his exact age, especially if he's close to turning 16 or 20.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Ah, I see - that makes sense. Well, I honestly don't know if he's in any approved education or training. He might be, or he might not be. I'm just not sure about his current situation with school or college either.

I realize this probably makes it difficult for you to tell me anything definite!

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're absolutely right - without knowing either Alex's exact age (whether he's under or over 16) or his education/training status, I'm unable to determine his eligibility for Child Benefit.

Here's what I need to make a proper assessment:

**At minimum, I need to know:**
1. **Whether Alex is under 16, or 16 and over** - this is the key age threshold
2. **If he's 16 or over:** Whether he's enrolled in approved education or training (such as A-levels, certain vocational courses, or approved training programs)

Child Benefit eligibility is determined on a per-child basis, and these details are essential to assess whether you can claim for Alex.

**Would you be able to find out this information and come back to me?** Once you have either his date of birth or can confirm his age relative to 16, plus his education/training status if he's 16+, I'll be able to give you a clear answer about your eligibility.

Is there anything else about the Child Benefit rules I can help clarify in the meantime?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
No, that's helpful - thank you. I understand now that I need to get his exact age sorted out and find out about his education status before you can tell me if I'm eligible. I'll gather that information and come back to you.

Thanks for your help!

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! Yes, once you have Alex's age (particularly whether he's under or over 16) and his education/training status if he's 16 or older, I'll be able to give you a clear answer on your eligibility for Child Benefit.

Feel free to come back anytime once you have that information - I'll be happy to help you complete the assessment.

Good luck, and take care!
